ideas.title: A boomerang that comes back
ideas.nearest: Skipping stones, a take that misses
same_form: Skipping stones, a take that misses
ideas.critique: It is one more thrown object filmed low over the island, and the last one of those missed. The difference is real, though: lift per blade element and the precession that comes out of it make a path nobody scripted, and a throw you have to catch is a skill toy people come back to. It only counts if the film clearly shows the loop and the catch, not a speck in the distance.

ideas.title: A rope you throw
ideas.critique: A rope wrapping round things has been done once already as a tangle of friends, so the wrap on its own will look familiar. What is new is a rod with friction against the real meshes and a swing the player rides. The risk is large: rod contact with Raycore meshes is hard, and a rope that clips through the branch kills the whole point.

ideas.title: Drawing with the sun
ideas.critique: Marks that stay on surfaces sit close to the human's own spray-can example, and a lens is a prop the island already used. Still, a refracted focal spot heating a heat grid until wood chars is a real chain of physics with a traced caustic at the end, and the height and clouds give the pen a feel. It stands or falls on whether the white star and the smoke read in the film.

ideas.title: A smoke ring cannon
ideas.critique: Nothing on the island has moved like this: a vortex filament driven by Biot-Savart induction is a real fluid model, and a slow, visible ring is something you can watch again and lead onto a target. The weak part is the payoff, knocking a hat off, which is small. Whether it lands depends on the smoke medium looking like a ring and not a grey blur.

ideas.title: Sky lanterns that really fly
ideas.critique: Night lights drifting over the island is a picture people expect, and the last night-light film missed. The buoyancy model is plain textbook (heat, ideal gas, drag), and the PrintSim sheet that fills with hot air is the only part with real depth. It is pretty, but there is little to play with after the first launch.

ideas.title: Keep the campfire alive
ideas.critique: Burning is named outright in the human's goals, so this is the expected way to carry it out, and as pitched the flame is a burn rate driving an emissive volume, not a fire simulation. A pile that collapses as its sticks thin out is the honest part, and tending the fire has a loop a player can follow.

ideas.title: Climb anything: the first real fall
ideas.critique: This is the third climbing post in a row that is a test, not a climb: a box tipping and a hold versus a slip on a beam is a debugging step, and the player still cannot climb anything. It is needed work, but as a post it repeats the same promise.

ideas.title: Dominoes across the meadow
ideas.critique: This is the domino chain the island already filmed, with mixed objects and a bell at the end. Real bodies are a step up, and placing your own pieces is a decent toy, but anyone who saw 'My day falls over' knows exactly what this looks like.

ideas.title: Gold leaf
ideas.critique: A thin sheet floating down and settling has been posted twice already. The new part is a conductor whose wrinkles break up the highlight until burnishing sharpens it, which suits the RayMakie material goal, but the play is slow and fiddly and the sheet itself is faked.

ideas.title: Tug of war in the mud
ideas.critique: A rhythm-tap mini game against the friends is the expected shape, like the earlier balancing game, and the physics is mu times weight on a chain. Mud stains that last until rain are a nice touch, but the core is a scripted contest with a simple friction rule under it.
